title: Salvage Ledger + Implicit Prefill Protocol for Paged KV Cache
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: The current paged-KV cache suffers from high fragmentation and costly full-page compactions during sustained mixed-length workloads. Prefill (warmup) traffic is conservative, which causes decode tail latency when kernels must rehydrate large KV fragments, and kernel selection currently lacks explicit hints about fragment quality.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight on-shard "Salvage Ledger" that tracks partial fragment metadata (valid token ranges, decay score, last-access epoch, salvageability) and an "Implicit Prefill Protocol" that opportunistically warms small high-salvage fragments during low-util periods or on speculative decode. Combine this with kernel-hint tags propagated from the scheduler to the kernel selector so kernels can prefer fast-paths when fragment continuity is high. The ledger enables low-overhead incremental compaction (salvage merges) and targeted eviction admissions rather than global page reclamation, reducing costly stalls.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end benchmark: 95th-percentile decode latency for mixed-burst workload reduced by >= 12% on representative 32k-context model compared to baseline without salvage ledger
KV memory reclaimed per hour via salvage merges without full-page compacts > 15% under synthetic fragmentation workload
No regressed CPU or GPU utilization beyond a 5% increase during background salvage (configurable throttle)
Kernel selector honors salvage/hotness tags and routes >= 80% of high-contiguity prefills to fast-path kernels in tests
Feature guarded and disabled by default; rollout to canary fleet (5%) with automatic rollback on error-rate or tail-latency regression
tasks: Design Salvage Ledger schema (compact metadata per fragment: fragment_id, token_range, continuity_score, last_touch_epoch, salvageable_flag)
Add on-shard ledger persistence + epoched reclamation API
Implement implicit prefill admission controller (budgeted, time-sliced) with backoff and tenant-weighting
Integrate kernel hint tags: extend request metadata and kernel selector mapping
Background salvage merge worker: incremental in-place stitch and micro-compact operations with preemption support
Unit tests for ledger correctness and continuity scoring
Microbench harness: synthetic fragmentation generator and mixed-length request replay
Performance validation on dedicated and hosted job profiles
Rollout playbook and observability dashboards (salvage rate, prefill budget usage, continuity histogram, tail latency)
Write migration/compatibility notes for shards without ledger state
decisions: Use a compact fixed-size per-fragment metadata record (<= 32 bytes) to limit memory overhead on shards
Continuity_score is computed from last N access ranges using an exponential decay so hot streaks matter more than old touches
Implicit prefill only warms fragments below a configurable token-size threshold (default 2 pages) to avoid large upfront reheats
Background salvage merges operate with a soft CPU/GPU throttle and can be paused when decode SLOs degrade
Kernel hint tags are advisory; kernel selector retains safety checks and fallback to generic kernel when needed
risks: Over-aggressive prefill could increase token-serving costs and GPU memory pressure if budget/tuning is incorrect
Incorrect continuity scoring may misclassify fragments and cause wasted merges
Adding metadata increases per-shard memory; need strict compact layout and evict older ledger entries
Race conditions between salvage merges and live decode writebacks require careful ordering and fencing
Cross-tenant fairness: salvage work must not favor noisy neighbors; admission controller must respect tenant weights
tests: Unit: ledger insertion/eviction, continuity scoring determinism
Integration: prefill admission + kernel hint roundtrip in staging cluster
Stress: synthetic 10k concurrent decodes with fragmentation pattern A/B to validate salvage rate and absence of stalls
Canary: deploy to 5% of runtime fleet with traffic shadowing and compare decode P50/P95/P99 against control
Chaos: simulate shard reboots mid-salvage to validate idempotency and ledger reconciliation
related_issues: ENG-221007 (microfusion kernel selector) - dependency for kernel hint integration
ENG-614200 (multi-tenant kv-snapshot warmup) - potential overlap on warmup admission logic
notes: Implementation should prefer additive feature flags controlled from console for tuning per-cluster and per-tenant settings
Prototype on a single shard showed a 9% P95 improvement with conservative prefill budget; further tuning expected
We will coordinate with solutions engineering before enabling for Dedicated customers due to cost sensitivity
